headlines.summary:

headlines.title_en: 10-year German Bund yield rises over 14 basis points in five days, hitting highest since 2011 intraday.
headlines.summary_en: At the tail end of European trading on Tuesday (Sept 1), Germany's 10-year Bund yield rose 2.0 basis points, marking a fifth consecutive session of gains (accumulating 14.3 bps over the period) to 3.344%, staying in positive territory throughout the day within a 3.325%-3.364% range, approaching the Q2 2011 high of 3.505% and the Q4 2008 peak of 4.148% at 17:41 Beijing time. The 2-year Schatz yield rose 2.6 bps, also up for five straight sessions (accumulating 15.2 bps) to 2.963%, trading within a 2.938%-2.971% intraday range; the 30-year Bund yield gained 0.5 bps to 3.817%, reaching 3.844% at 17:51, nearing the Q2 2011 high of 3.980% and the Q1 2010 top of 4.14%.

headlines.title: 李斌：下半年单车成本至少再涨2000元
headlines.summary: “今年中国汽车市场的压力非常大，但是蔚来整个公司的增长质量非常高。”9月1日晚间，蔚来创始人、董事长、CEO李斌在蔚来2026年第二季度财报电话会上表示。展望下半年，李斌认为，整体汽车市场将在第四季度有所恢复，蔚来公司在第四季度的目标是每个月实现4万辆以上的交付量。长期来看，希望每年有40%-50%的年销量增长。李斌预计，今年下半年，每辆车的成本还将继续上涨2000到3000元。即相较于去年年底，每辆车的成本将增长1.6万-1.7万元。（澎湃）

headlines.title_en: Li Bin: Per-vehicle cost to rise at least RMB 2,000 in H2.
headlines.summary_en: NIO's founder, chairman and CEO William Li said at the company's Q2 2026 earnings call on the evening of Sept 1: "The pressure on China's auto market this year is immense, but NIO's overall growth quality is very high." Looking ahead to H2, Li believes the overall auto market will recover in Q4, with NIO targeting monthly deliveries above 40,000 vehicles in the fourth quarter. Over the long term, he hopes for annual sales growth of 40%-50%. Li expects per-vehicle costs to continue rising by 2,000-3,000 yuan in H2, bringing cumulative cost increases per vehicle to 16,000-17,000 yuan versus end of last year. (The Paper)

headlines.title: 美国公布贝森特与植田和男会谈纪录，美方暗示支持央行出手撑日元

headlines.title_en: US releases record of Bessent-Ueda meeting; US signals support for central bank intervention to bolster yen.
headlines.summary_en: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has repeatedly signaled that Japan needs to raise interest rates to support the yen. After meeting with Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda, he further signaled support for such a move. According to meeting minutes released by the Treasury on Tuesday, Bessent "strongly supported Japan's decisive market and monetary policy actions to address the clearly undervalued yen exchange rate," also noting that yen weakness was intensifying domestic inflationary pressures in Japan. The meeting took place on Sunday in Asheville, North Carolina, where both were attending the G20 finance ministers and central bank governors meeting.
